# Data Health checks and reports

Data Health monitors individual resources with checks for status, freshness, size, content, and schema. For example, a build status check asks whether the most recent build of a dataset succeeded. A check is the saved rule; each evaluation produces a check report with a result and a snapshot of the rule at that time. Time-based checks can evaluate on dataset updates, at configured thresholds, or on a regular schedule. Creation alone need not produce a report, so `get-latest` may return an empty collection until evaluation occurs. A failed check reports unhealthy data, while an API failure means the request itself could not complete. See [Health checks](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/health-checks/overview), [check evaluation](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/health-checks/check-evaluation), the [checks reference](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/health-checks/checks-reference).

The examples assume valid Foundry credentials and the required dataset or check permissions. Replace sample RIDs. A `buildStatus` rule uses a dataset RID, branch, and severity (`MODERATE` or `CRITICAL`). Other rule types have different configuration fields; inspect their SDK model before editing the JSON.

## Read and query objects

An **object set** is a collection of objects defined by a type and optional filters, links, or other operations. It can be evaluated to fetch objects or aggregated to answer questions such as counts by status. Query only the fields and result scope the application needs; large traversals and aggregations consume Ontology query capacity. Distinguish a dynamic object-set expression from a saved, static selection when choosing whether results should follow later data changes. See [Object Set basics](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/ontologies-v2-resources/ontology-object-sets/ontology-object-set-basics), [saved Object Sets](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/analytics/datasets-object-sets), and [query compute](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/ontologies/query-compute-usage).

For application code, use the [TypeScript OSDK query model](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/ontology-sdk/typescript-osdk) for object reads, links, filters, and aggregations. Inside Foundry Functions, object-set APIs support searches and aggregation; the [Functions Object Sets reference](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/functions/api-object-sets) describes the TypeScript v1 form, so check the [language feature matrix](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/functions/language-feature-support) before translating an example to TypeScript v2 or Python. A shipment queue, for instance, can filter `Shipment` objects by status, follow their warehouse links, and aggregate by destination instead of loading every object into application memory.

An **Action** is the operational write boundary. Define typed [parameters](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/parameter-overview), [rules](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/rules) that create or edit objects and links, [submission criteria](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/submission-criteria) that validate when it may run, and [permissions](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/permissions) that control who may apply it. For a `Dispatch shipment` action, parameters might include a shipment and destination; criteria can reject an invalid state before rules edit its status and link. Read and write authorizations govern what data action logic can access and change; application UI checks do not replace these controls. See [Action overview](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/overview) and [read/write authorizations](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/read-write-authorizations).

Use a [function-backed Action](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/function-actions-overview) when rules need code-based logic, and inspect its edit scope before publishing. A side-effect webhook runs after object changes and may complete after the user sees success. Design external consumers for retries and reconciliation; neither mode promises one atomic transaction across Foundry and the external system. [Side effects](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/side-effects-overview) also include other post-submission behaviors.

The platform SDK also exposes Ontology endpoints, including metadata such as object types and action types. The installed `pal_found_cli` is another interface with its own supported command set; an API endpoint appearing here does not imply a corresponding CLI command.

## Host, version, and endpoint

Send requests to the HTTPS hostname of the target Foundry enrollment, followed by `/api/v2/...` or the version shown on the endpoint page. For example, [Get Dataset](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/datasets-v2-resources/datasets/get-dataset) is `GET /api/v2/datasets/{datasetRid}` and is marked Stable in the Python SDK's v2 method reference. A dataset RID identifies the resource; its display name does not replace the RID in this path. Find the hostname in the browser URL for that enrollment. [Getting started](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/general/overview/getting-started) explains the host and first request.

The major API version is part of the URL. A change from v1 to v2 can change request or response contracts. Within a major version, clients must tolerate additions such as response fields and enum values. Check an endpoint's release stage and deprecation notice before depending on it. [Versioning](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/general/overview/versioning) describes these guarantees.

Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. ## Errors, throttling, and retries

Foundry errors use HTTP `4xx` or `5xx` status codes and a JSON body with `errorCode`, `errorName`, `errorInstanceId`, and `parameters`. Record the instance ID when diagnosing a failed call. A `404` may mean the resource is missing or the caller cannot access it, as [Get Dataset](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/datasets-v2-resources/datasets/get-dataset) states. Fix invalid input, authentication, or permissions before retrying a `400`, `401`, or `403`. The [error reference](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/general/overview/errors) lists operation-specific errors.

Foundry can throttle calls with `429` or `503`; [API limits](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/general/overview/limits) recommends exponential backoff. Bound retry count and concurrency. Before retrying a create, upload, Action, or other write after a timeout, check its operation semantics and whether the first attempt may already have succeeded. Blind replay can produce duplicate effects.
